vectors.name: compat/basic/adding-optional-field-narrows-forward
vectors.comment: A may emit `nick`; B is closed and has no such field. Readers holding B would break.

vectors.name: compat/basic/adding-optional-field-widens-backward
vectors.comment: The same pair, arguments reversed. Direction is the whole question.

vectors.name: compat/basic/adding-required-field-is-not-accepted-by-old
vectors.comment: Clause 2 of record_sub: B requires `email` with min 1 and A does not guarantee it.

vectors.name: compat/scalar/date-is-not-a-subtype-of-datetime
vectors.comment: integer/number is the ONLY subtyping relation. This vector exists to stop a fourth implementation from adding a second one.

vectors.name: compat/cardinality/unbounded-does-not-fit-bounded
vectors.comment: Also pins the comma-first cardinality form [,5], which the OSD grammar accepts.

vectors.name: compat/recursion/coinduction-terminates-on-mutual-refs
vectors.comment: Recursive on both sides. An implementation without memoized coinduction does not terminate here.

vectors.name: compat/satisfiability/unsatisfiable-a-is-vacuously-a-subschema
vectors.comment: A accepts no finite document, so every document it accepts is trivially accepted by B.

vectors.name: equivalent/renaming-records-preserves-equivalence
vectors.comment: Equivalence is about accepted documents, never about record names or declaration order.
